description: Mitigations for confined space and breathing hazards. Rescue capability is the dominant post-impact control — 60% of confined space deaths are rescuers.

mitigations.name: elimination_entry
mitigations.description: Design out the need for confined space entry. Remote inspection (cameras, drones), external cleaning systems, automation. If no one enters, no one dies.
mitigations.pfd_source: Inherent safety. PFD reflects rare cases where entry is still needed despite design intent.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Complete elimination of the breathing hazard if no entry occurs.

mitigations.name: continuous_monitoring
mitigations.description: Fixed or portable multi-gas detector (O2, LEL, CO, H2S) with alarm. Continuous monitoring during entry — alerts worker before atmosphere becomes IDLH.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Failure: not calibrated, sensor poisoned, alarm ignored, battery dead, placed in wrong location within the space.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Early warning allows self-rescue before incapacitation. Most effective when alarm triggers immediate evacuation. Ineffective if atmosphere changes suddenly (e.g., argon purge initiated during entry).

mitigations.name: forced_ventilation
mitigations.description: Mechanical ventilation diluting/displacing hazardous atmosphere. Blower + ducting providing fresh air to the space. Must run continuously during entry.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.07. Failure: insufficient air changes, duct disconnected, blower tripped, intake contaminated, space geometry prevents effective ventilation (dead spots).
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Effective for displacing accumulated gas/vapour. Less effective for oxygen-displacing inert gas (heavier-than-air gases settle below duct level). Continuous operation is critical.

mitigations.name: scba
mitigations.description: Self-contained breathing apparatus providing independent air supply. Worker breathes from cylinder regardless of ambient atmosphere. The definitive pre-impact control for IDLH atmospheres.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.10. Failure: mask seal failure (facial hair), cylinder duration exceeded, not donned correctly, worker removes mask in space.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When properly worn, provides complete respiratory protection regardless of atmosphere. Duration limited by cylinder (typically 30-45 min). Very high effectiveness when working.

mitigations.name: permit_confined_space
mitigations.description: Formal permit system per 29 CFR 1910.146 / CS Regs 1997. Pre-entry atmosphere test, ventilation, rescue plan, attendant, communication. The framework that ensures other controls are in place.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: A permit alone doesn't change the atmosphere — it ensures monitoring, ventilation, SCBA, and rescue are in place. Effectiveness is indirect.

mitigations.name: standby_rescue_team
mitigations.description: Trained, SCBA-equipped rescue team positioned at the confined space entry during all work. Can effect rescue within 5 minutes of alarm. THE critical post-impact control — without it, confined space collapse is almost always fatal.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.10. Failure: team not on standby (called away, shift change), SCBA not ready, untrained bystander attempts rescue instead (60% of deaths are rescuers).
mitigations.effectiveness_source: HSE data: rescue within 5 min dramatically improves survival from O2-deficient atmosphere. Brain damage begins at 4 min without oxygen. The rescue team transforms P(death) from ~0.90 to ~0.20.

mitigations.name: retrieval_line
mitigations.description: Non-entry rescue capability: worker wears harness attached to retrieval line on tripod/davit at entry point. Attendant can extract the worker without entering the space. Eliminates the rescuer-becomes-victim cascade.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.12. Failure: not attached, line tangled in space, space geometry prevents extraction (bends, obstructions), worker too heavy for manual retrieval.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When the geometry allows extraction, retrieval is fast (seconds to minutes). Eliminates the need for a rescuer to enter. Effectiveness limited by space configuration.

sources.author: HSE
sources.relevance: Confined Spaces Regulations 1997 — ACOP and guidance. 60% of deaths are rescuers.

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Permit-Required Confined Spaces 29 CFR 1910.146. Most cited for rescue plan failures.

sources.author: CCPS
sources.relevance: LOPA guidelines — PFD for monitoring, ventilation, SCBA, rescue.
